title: Isolation Forest
subtitle: Recursive Random Partitioning for Anomaly Detection
summary: Isolate anomalies in fewer random axis splits than dense normal points.

evaluationChart.title: Anomaly Score Distribution Histogram
evaluationChart.description: Separates normal inliers (scores < 0.55) from isolated outliers (scores approaching 1.0).

advantages: Linear O(t · ψ · log ψ) time complexity with tiny memory footprint.
Requires no distance or density matrix calculation; scales to high dimensions.
Directly targets anomaly isolation rather than profiling normal density.
limitations: Axis-aligned splits can miss diagonal anomalies or create 'ghost' artifacts.
Requires tuning contamination threshold for binary alerting.
Local anomalies inside multi-modal clusters can be masked.
applications: Real-time credit card fraud & intrusion detection

formulas.label: Isolation Anomaly Score
formulas.description: Shorter average path length E(h(x)) yields score s -> 1 (anomaly); longer paths yield s < 0.5.

hyperparameters.label: Isolation Trees (t)
hyperparameters.description: Number of random isolation trees in the ensemble.

hyperparameters.label: Score Threshold
hyperparameters.description: Anomaly score cutoff flagging red outlier points.

codeTemplates.scikitLearn:
from sklearn.ensemble import IsolationForest
import numpy as np

X = np.array([[4.5,4.8],[5.0,5.1],[4.7,4.5],[1.2,8.4],[8.7,1.6]])
iso = IsolationForest(contamination=0.2, random_state=42)
print('Predictions (1=inlier, -1=outlier):', iso.fit_predict(X))
